sections.overview: This deepwater dogfish is listed as Etmopterus baxteri by the New Zealand Organisms Register, while the Australian CAAB catalogue treats that name as a synonym of E. granulosus following a taxonomic revision. Older ecological records under either name should therefore be read with their taxonomic usage in mind.
sections.identification: The New Zealand guide describes a stout, uniformly dark shark with randomly spaced dermal denticles; it contrasts with E. lucifer, whose denticles form linear rows, and E. pusillus, which has smoother skin.
sections.habitat: Records place it around New Zealand and Australia on deep continental slopes, extending to about 1500 m in the New Zealand guide.
sections.diet: A study off Tasmania found teleost fishes to be its main prey, with cephalopods also frequent and crustaceans a minor component; these results describe the sampled Australian population.
sections.behavior: The guide does not describe its activity.
sections.reproduction: The guide gives no breeding details.
sections.ecology: It is a slope-dwelling predator that appears in New Zealand deepwater fisheries as non-target catch; this documents fishery interaction, not a population trend.
sections.conservation: The fisheries report documents bycatch but does not assess this shark’s global conservation status or population trend.
